stem:
Calcium chloride, $\text{CaCl}_2$, is an ionic solid.

The values of some energy changes are shown in Table 1.1.

Table 1.1

| energy change | value/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| lattice energy, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{latt}}$, $\text{CaCl}_2\text{(s)}$ | $-2237$ |
| standard enthalpy change of atomisation of calcium | $+193$ |
| first ionisation energy of calcium | $+590$ |
| second ionisation energy of calcium | $+1150$ |
| standard enthalpy change of atomisation of chlorine | $+121$ |
| first electron affinity of chlorine | $-364$ |

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Use the data in Table 1.1 to calculate the standard enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{f}}$, of calcium chloride. It may be helpful to draw an energy cycle. Show all your working.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Three possible values for the first electron affinity of bromine are shown in Table 1.2. One of them is correct.

Place a tick by the correct value. Explain your choice.

Table 1.2

| possible values | place **one** tick (✓) in this column |
| :--- | :--- |
| $-342\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ |  |
| $-364\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ |  |
| $-386\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ |  |

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
The enthalpy change of hydration of the chloride ion can be calculated using the lattice energy of calcium chloride and the data shown in Table 1.3.

Table 1.3

| energy change | value/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| standard enthalpy change of solution of $\text{CaCl}_2\text{(s)}$ | $-83$ |
| standard enthalpy change of hydration of $\text{Ca}^{2+}\text{(g)}$ | $-1650$ |

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the standard enthalpy change of hydration of the chloride ion, $\text{Cl}^-\text{(g)}$. It may be helpful to draw an energy cycle. Show all your working.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem:
Calcium fluoride, $\text{CaF}_2\text{(s)}$, can be synthesised directly from its elements.

The value of $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{f}}(\text{CaF}_2\text{(s)})$ is $-1214\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
parts.text: Predict the sign of the entropy change, $\Delta S^\ominus$, for this synthesis. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Use the value of $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{f}}(\text{CaF}_2\text{(s)})$ given in (e) and your answer to (e)(i) to predict how the feasibility for this synthesis will change with increasing temperature.
